Hi Hannah —

Quick note from FinRipple's privacy team: we were notified today that Redwood plans to add a temporary telemetry processor (EdgeScope Inc.) to the processing roster for low-latency telemetry in us-west. Before we update our records and sign the amendment, two asks: 1) confirmation of whether EdgeScope will receive plaintext request/response bodies or only scrubbed telemetry; 2) the retention window Redwood will apply to logs that flow through EdgeScope (we need the max and the default values).

We'd also appreciate any export/control/rollback plan if EdgeScope is removed within 30–60 days — specifically how long artifacts stay on their systems and whether Redwood will request deletion certificates. Can you point us to the minimal evidence package your legal/privacy team will share?

We'd like to close this out by next Wednesday if possible. Attaching a placeholder POA that lists the fields we care about.

Thanks,
Elaine

Hi Elaine — thanks for the ping and the clear asks. Looping in Kim (legal/DPA) and Marcus (infra) to confirm the technical and contractual pieces. High level: EdgeScope will be used only for telemetry aggregation (metrics, anonymized request traces) and we do not intend to route unredacted customer content there. That said, I want confirmatory detail on the exact fields that may be present in logs.

Kim/Marcus — can you please confirm: (A) whether any plaintext request/response bodies might be present in the telemetry we forward to EdgeScope under any failure mode; (B) the retention window we will set by default vs. the maximum retention we can commit to in an addendum; (C) an export/rollback checklist (what we ask EdgeScope to purge and how we get confirmation). Elaine asked for a deletion certificate example, and a short evidence packet for procurement.

Elaine — we'll aim to provide a concise evidence bundle by EOD Tue. If we need more time for legal sign-off we'll propose a concrete timeline.

— Hannah

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2024 12:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor propagation and conditional retention inquiry

Thanks Hannah. Quick summary from legal: we can produce an addendum to the DPA that enumerates EdgeScope's permitted processing activities and retention caps. Draft attached (Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf).

Answers to Elaine's initial questions: 
- Access to plaintext request/response bodies: contractually, EdgeScope will be limited to telemetry aggregates and sampling of anonymized traces. We will include a clause that forbids access to customer payloads and requires immediate notification if any plaintext is observed.
- Retention: default retention will be 14 days for telemetry traces; maximum retention we will propose in the addendum is 90 days with explicit customer opt-in.
- Removal/rollback: we will require deletion certificates within 30 days of termination and include a short attestation template.

Attaching the addendum and a lightweight evidence checklist. Marcus — please add the dataflow sketch and the operational controls we will include, then I'll route to FinRipple.

(attachments: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf, evidence-checklist.txt)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2024 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor propagation and conditional retention inquiry

Adding the infra / ops perspective — see inline and attached diagram. Key technical points: 
- We will only forward metric and sampling traces to EdgeScope. No full request payloads are routed in normal operation. 
- Failure modes: if the tracing agent misconfigures, sample headers may expose customer identifiers. To mitigate, sampling excludes full payload capture and we have an agent-level guard that strips bodies. We will include logs from the agent showing body-stripping enforcement in the evidence packet.
- Retention enforcement: EdgeScope will be configured with TTL policies; default TTL 14d, retention_max=90d. Any customer-facing opt-ins that increase retention will require a signed addendum and a feature flag that we can audit.

I've attached: dataflow-diagram-v2.png (sketch of telemetry path), subprocessor-entry-log.csv (audit of onboarding checks). I'm scheduling a brief runbook update to capture deletion certificate request steps.

—Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachments: dataflow-diagram-v2.png, subprocessor-entry-log.csv)
